criteria.check: Every number, result or specific claim attributed to a published work cites that work and the page or section it comes from, and the cited passage in the evidence supports it.

Results of different works are compared as better or worse only when they share the dataset or benchmark, the metric and the protocol, and the answer says so; otherwise the answer states that the numbers are not directly comparable.
The answer separates what a cited work demonstrates from what the review itself infers or proposes, with wording that marks the latter (for example "we propose", "this suggests").
Results from one version of a paper or system are not presented as properties of a later version, product or deployment unless the evidence covers that version.
When the answer draws conclusions about a field, it says how the works discussed were chosen and that the selection is not exhaustive when it is not.
